title: What to watch on Day 15 of the Winter Olympics: Eileen Gu goes for gold, U.S. bobsledders chase more medals
content:
The Athletic has live coverage of the 2026 Winter Olympics.

It feels like only yesterday that a Norwegian skier bore his heart on the medal stand.

Alas, the final weekend of the Milan Cortina Winter Olympics is here, and we have only two more days to chide cheaters, toast virtuosity and rue what could’ve been at these glorious Games.

At least the Winter Olympics are about to go out with a bang, starting with an epic Saturday that features 12 events with medals up for grabs. That includes a dramatic men’s curling tournament coming to a close, the American women going for another bobsled medal, and the halfpipe producing one more night of aerial artistry in Livigno.

Then we get a gold medal game for the ages in men’s hockey early Sunday morning (in North America, anyway). Set those alarm clocks now. (Here’s a schedule of events.)

Times: 2:40 p.m. ET, 8:40 p.m. in Italy
TV: Peacock

What to watch for: The Finns couldn’t finish against Canada in Friday’s semifinals. Now they must play for bronze against Slovakia, a surprise group winner in the preliminary round that was hammered 6-2 by the Americans in the semifinals. Slovakia is going for its second straight bronze medal after beating Sweden in a Beijing Games tournament that did not include NHL players, and Finland is looking to medal for the fifth time in the last six Games.

Montreal Canadiens winger Juraj Slafkovský is tied for fourth in the men’s tournament with 8 points (four goals, four assists) for Slovakia. Dallas Stars winger Mikko Rantanen leads Finland with 6 points (two goals, four assists), including the opening goal in the Finns’ 3-2 loss to Canada.

Times: 8:05 a.m. ET, 2:05 p.m. in Italy
TV: Peacock

What to watch for: The Americans get a second chance to clinch the first women’s curling medal in U.S. history after a semifinal loss to Switzerland on Friday. The Canadians’ five-match winning streak ended in a 6-3 semifinal loss to Sweden, and now they face an American team that beat them in round-robin play 9-8. If Saturday’s bronze medal game is anything like their round-robin match — a wild affair that saw the lead change hands on each of the last two ends — then we’re in for a treat.

Times: 1:05 p.m. ET, 7:05 p.m. in Italy
TV: Peacock

What to watch for: A Canadian curling team hounded by cheating accusations earlier in the tournament is one win from the country’s first gold medal in men’s curling since the Sochi Games in 2014. Great Britain is in the gold medal game for the second consecutive Olympics and is now looking to finish the job after beating the Swiss 8-5 in Thursday’s semifinals. Marc Kennedy, the man who cursed out the Swedes in a tense round-robin match last week, is going for his second gold medal and third overall. He led the Canadians to gold in the Vancouver Games in 2010 and took bronze in Beijing in 2022.

Times: 1 p.m. ET, 7 p.m. in Italy
TV: Peacock

What to watch for: Kaillie Humphries is in line for her second medal of the Milan Cortina Games after she and partner Jasmine Jones posted the third-best combined time in the first two heats of two-woman bobsled Friday. The 40-year-old Humphries claimed bronze in the monobob earlier in the Games for the fifth Olympic medal of her career. She and Jones are 0.23 seconds behind leaders Laura Nolte and Deborah Levi of Germany with two runs to go. Fellow Americans Kaysha Love and Azaria Hill are in fifth, 0.62 seconds back of the lead.

Times: 1:30 p.m. ET, 7:30 p.m. in Italy
TV: Peacock

What to watch for: What better way to close out Livigno Snow Park than with China’s Eileen Gu aiming for gold on the halfpipe? Gu has two silver medals in the Games (big air and slopestyle) and will attempt to successfully defend her gold medal in this event from the 2022 Winter Olympics. Great Britain’s Zoe Atkin is the defending world champion and is looking to follow in her sister Izzy’s footsteps after the latter won a freeski bronze at Pyeongchang in 2018.
